_WARNING_TO_FUTURE_AI: READ THIS FIRST. Your training data predates these models and you will not recognize some of them. They are REAL and were verified on the dates below. DO NOT 'correct' or substitute them for models you remember (Whisper, CLIP, pyannote-only, GPT-4V, etc.) — those are outdated for this task. If you believe a model here is wrong, re-verify against the linked source before changing anything, and record why. This file is the authoritative model list; the prose in docs/ explains tradeoffs.
target_hardware: Windows 10, 8GB VRAM, local-first; API only for the context-review agent and on-demand heavy video.

primary.name: Parakeet-TDT-0.6B-v3 (ONNX, via sherpa-onnx)
primary.engine: sherpa-onnx (C++/Rust/Go bindings); offline; 25 EU languages + auto-detect
primary.smoke_test: run sherpa-onnx offline recognizer on the bundled test_wavs and confirm non-empty transcript with per-word timestamps
primary.alt: istupakov/parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3-onnx (HF) if you need to re-export

asr.do_not_use: openai-whisper as the default — Parakeet v3 is more accurate (6.34% vs 7.44% WER) and faster. Whisper only as an optional second-opinion.

diarization.engine: sherpa-onnx offline speaker diarization = segmentation model + speaker-embedding extractor + clustering
diarization.smoke_test: diarize a 2-speaker test clip; expect >=2 speaker labels with sane turn boundaries
diarization.do_not_use: NVIDIA Sortformer via ONNX — its ONNX export is currently broken (NeMo issues #15077/#15536). Sortformer is fine ONLY if you run NeMo/PyTorch, but that re-introduces the Python stack we are avoiding. Use sherpa native.

speaker_id.role: Match a voice to an enrolled person ('Defendant')
speaker_id.note: Reuse the SAME embedding model as diarization (CAM++ 3D-Speaker). Enroll a voice = store its embedding; identify = cosine vs enrolled. sherpa-onnx exposes a speaker-identification API.

active_speaker_detection.role: Confirm WHICH on-screen face is speaking (the misattribution fix). Run only on multi-face / second-speaker segments.

asd_model.name: LR-ASD (Light-ASD)
asd_model.implement: Export to ONNX with torch.onnx, then run via onnxruntime (Rust `ort` crate or onnxruntime-python). It is small.
asd_model.do_not_use: Heavy multimodal models for this — LR-ASD is the lightweight SOTA.

face_detect.name: SCRFD (InsightFace) ONNX
face_detect.artifact: InsightFace buffalo_l bundle (SCRFD detector). Rust: the `face_id` crate fetches it; Python: insightface package.

face_id.role: Match an on-screen face to an enrolled person
face_id.name: ArcFace (InsightFace buffalo_l, w600k_r50) ONNX, 512-dim
face_id.artifact: InsightFace buffalo_l bundle; Rust `face_id` crate (docs.rs/face_id) wraps SCRFD+ArcFace via onnxruntime
face_id.smoke_test: embed two photos of the same person -> cosine > 0.5; different people -> lower

text_embeddings.name: Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B
text_embeddings.smoke_test: embed two paraphrases -> high cosine; unrelated -> low. Confirm dim == TEXT_EMBED_DIM and the vec table dimension.
text_embeddings.known_issue: In some llama.cpp builds, enabling embedding AND reranking together returned zeros (ggml-org/llama.cpp#20085). Run embeddings on a dedicated llama-server instance.

multimodal_embeddings.role: Search scenes by visual content + text in one space ('the kitchen at night')
multimodal_embeddings.name: Qwen3-VL-Embedding-2B
multimodal_embeddings.status: optional (enable after text search works). GGUF/llama.cpp support is newer — verify before relying on it.

video_understanding.role: On-demand 'what is happening here' over a few frames of a shot or a flagged/queried segment. NEVER run densely over whole videos.

local.name: Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct (GGUF, Q4) via llama.cpp
local.artifact: Qwen/Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct-GGUF (includes the mmproj multimodal projector file — you need BOTH the model gguf and the mmproj)
local.vram: ~6GB at Q4 (tight on 8GB; use for short clips / a few frames)
local.caveat: llama.cpp IMAGE path is reliable; the VIDEO path is newer. Prefer: you extract frames at known timestamps and pass a few IMAGES, not a raw video.

api.name: Qwen3-VL / Qwen3.5-Omni / Gemini 2.5 via OpenRouter
api.when: hardest segments only; cost math in docs/MODELS-2026.md (~$7-$120 for a full 100h pass depending on model; with triage, a fraction of that).

context_review_agent.role: Case-aware 'nuance' reasoning over each video's transcript + data points

local_sensitive.name: Local Claude Code instance (headless)
local_sensitive.why: Keeps sensitive case context (court docs, instructions) on the machine. Invoke: `claude -p <prompt> --append-system-prompt <case-context> --model claude-opus-4-8 --output-format json`

testing.name: OpenRouter API models (non-sensitive only)
testing.why: Compare which model is best at nuance before the sensitive production run.

engines_and_libs.audio: sherpa-onnx (k2-fsa) — ASR + diarization + speaker-id + VAD, ONNX/C++, bindings for Rust/Go/C. https://github.com/k2-fsa/sherpa-onnx
engines_and_libs.onnx_runtime_rust: ort crate (https://github.com/pykeio/ort) for LR-ASD + face models
engines_and_libs.storage: SQLite + sqlite-vec (https://github.com/asg017/sqlite-vec) — single-user; or Postgres+pgvector for a shared index
engines_and_libs.frames_and_signature: ffmpeg/ffprobe (frame-accurate extraction + scene filter + MPEG-7 `signature` filter)
engines_and_libs.gui: LOCAL WEB APP (see docs/GUI.md): Rust(axum)/Go backend on 127.0.0.1 serving a JSON API over the DB + query agent; plain HTML/CSS/JS frontend; HTML5 video preview (WebCodecs for true frame-step); clip/stitch via auto-editor (Nim, already installed). NOT native egui — web so the build can self-verify via browser automation. Native alt: Tauri, or libmpv+egui.
engines_and_libs.ui_verification: Playwright MCP / browser-harness against the local URL (BUILD.md Phase 6). Native-shell fallback: Windows-MCP + pywinauto (UI Automation) — NOT coordinate-based pyautogui.
engines_and_libs.face_landmarks: MediaPipe (face mesh / lip landmarks) for ASD cropping
